instruction: This flowgraph runs at a sample rate of 48 kHz and simulates a receiver recording with weak and strong bursts: a complex 1.2 kHz tone (amplitude 0.5) is multiplied by a repeating burst envelope (4000 samples at 0.1, then 4000 samples at 3.0), passed through an AGC and written as complex samples to rx.dat. The AGC reacts far too slowly. Retune it, changing parameter values only, so that from 240 samples (5 ms) after every level change until the next change, rx.dat has an RMS level of 1.0 within 10 %, both over the first 240 samples of that stretch and over the rest of it. The 1.2 kHz tone must stay clean: in each of those stretches its strongest component is at 1.2 kHz (within 1 %), and at least 99 % of the power lies within 50 Hz of it. Do not change the tone or the burst envelope. Save the flowgraph. It should keep producing samples until it is stopped.

instruction: This flowgraph runs at a sample rate of 48 kHz. It rectifies a 50 Hz test tone whose amplitude is 2.0 for half a second and 1.0 for the next half second, repeating, and writes the rectified signal as float samples to rectified.dat. Add an Embedded Python block after the rectifier that holds the peak: for every input sample it outputs the largest value among that sample and the 959 samples before it (960 samples, one period of the 50 Hz tone). Write its output as float samples to a new File Sink with the file name peak.dat, and keep rectified.dat as it is. Save the flowgraph. It should keep producing samples until it is stopped.
